pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes that workflow emails are still sent for cancelled and rescheduled bookings. The fix of PR #6991 was wrong and didn't work as expected. 

The SendGrid endpoint `DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/${referenceId}` was not used correctly. This endpoint deletes a cancelled scheduled email from `scheduled_sends` by removing the 'cancel' status (so email will again be scheduled). 

The reason why cancelling our scheduled emails stopped working is that all cancerlled emails are saved in `scheduled_sends` until the scheduled date but the max. of pending cancellations is 100. Once we reached 100 pending cancellations, new cancellations failed and emails were still sent out. 

The solution implemented in this PR: 
- A new field `cancelled` is added to the `workflowReminder` model
- Once an already scheduled email is cancelled, the field is set to true (nothing else is done at this point in time)
- The CRON job `scheduleEmailReminders` is responsible for the final cancellation of the scheduled email (runs every 15 mins)
  - cancels all scheduled emails that are cancelled and that have their scheduled date within the next hour

Fixes #7225

**Environment**: Staging(main branch) / Production

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Chore (refactoring code, technical debt, workflow improvements)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update
pr.title: Fixes that workflow reminders of cancelled and rescheduled bookings are still sent

raw_findings.body: The catch exits the entire loop: all subsequent reminders in `remindersToCancel` are never cancelled at SendGrid in this run, and the already-pushed but not-yet-awaited PrismaPromise deletes never execute (Prisma queries only run when awaited). If the failing reminder sorts early on every run, other cancelled bookings' reminder emails are still sent once their send time passes.
raw_findings.failure_mode: One bad reminder poisons the batch: remaining cancellations are skipped and DB cleanup for already-cancelled reminders silently never runs.
raw_findings.impact: The catch exits the entire loop: all subsequent reminders in `remindersToCancel` are never cancelled at SendGrid in this run, and the already-pushed but not-yet-awaited PrismaPromise deletes never execute (Prisma queries only run when awaited). If the failing reminder sorts early on every run, other cancelled bookings' reminder emails are still sent once their send time passes.
raw_findings.root_cause: New CRON cancellation block wraps the whole per-reminder loop, including deferred lazy Prisma deletes, in one try/catch instead of isolating failures per reminder.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Move the try/catch inside the for-loop so each reminder is cancelled/deleted independently, and await (or explicitly execute) the delete per iteration instead of deferring all deletes to a single Promise.all after the loop.
raw_findings.title: Single try/catch around SendGrid cancellation loop aborts all remaining cancellations on first failure
raw_findings.trigger: The CRON runs with multiple `cancelled: true` reminders pending and one SendGrid cancel request fails (e.g., expired/invalid batch referenceId, 100-pending-cancellation limit, transient API error) partway through the loop.

raw_findings.body: This path performs the immediate SendGrid `status: "cancel"` POST that this PR identifies as the root cause of the original bug (pending cancellations accumulate until the scheduled date, capping at 100, after which cancellations fail). When the call fails, nothing marks the row `cancelled` or deletes it, so the CRON never picks it up and the old booking's reminder email is still sent. Even on success, the workflowReminder row is left with `scheduled: true` and no `cancelled` flag until the top-of-CRON deleteMany prunes it.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Rescheduled bookings can still receive stale workflow reminder emails once SendGrid's pending-cancellation limit is hit, silently defeating the fix for this code path.
raw_findings.impact: This path performs the immediate SendGrid `status: "cancel"` POST that this PR identifies as the root cause of the original bug (pending cancellations accumulate until the scheduled date, capping at 100, after which cancellations fail). When the call fails, nothing marks the row `cancelled` or deletes it, so the CRON never picks it up and the old booking's reminder email is still sent. Even on success, the workflowReminder row is left with `scheduled: true` and no `cancelled` flag until the top-of-CRON deleteMany prunes it.
raw_findings.root_cause: Inconsistent use of the new `immediateDelete` flag: the booking-page reschedule path retains the immediate SendGrid cancel pattern the PR was written to eliminate.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete` here (as done in handleCancelBooking and bookings.tsx requestReschedule) so the reminder is flagged `cancelled: true` and reliably cancelled by the CRON close to its send time.
raw_findings.title: Reschedule path in handleNewBooking uses immediateDelete=true, bypassing the new deferred-cancellation mechanism and leaving the reminder row stale
raw_findings.trigger: A booking with a scheduled email workflow reminder (referenceId set, send date possibly days away) is rescheduled via the booking page; SendGrid's pending-cancellation queue is near its 100-item limit or the cancel request fails.

raw_findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder only sets `cancelled: true` and relies entirely on the CRON; if the reminder's send time falls before the next CRON execution, the top-of-handler deleteMany (scheduledDate <= now) removes the row without ever issuing the SendGrid cancel, and the reminder email is delivered for a cancelled booking — the exact symptom this PR fixes, now for last-minute cancellations. The previous code cancelled immediately and did not have this window.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Attendees/hosts still receive workflow reminder emails for bookings cancelled at the last minute.
raw_findings.impact: deleteScheduledEmailReminder only sets `cancelled: true` and relies entirely on the CRON; if the reminder's send time falls before the next CRON execution, the top-of-handler deleteMany (scheduledDate <= now) removes the row without ever issuing the SendGrid cancel, and the reminder email is delivered for a cancelled booking — the exact symptom this PR fixes, now for last-minute cancellations. The previous code cancelled immediately and did not have this window.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new deferred-cancellation design assumes the CRON will always run between the cancellation event and the reminder's send time, which is false for cancellations occurring within one CRON period of the send time.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: In deleteScheduledEmailReminder, additionally issue an immediate SendGrid cancel when scheduledDate is within the CRON interval (or process cancelled reminders before the deleteMany and widen/reorder logic so imminent sends are cancelled synchronously).
raw_findings.title: Reminders cancelled less than one CRON interval before their send time are never cancelled at SendGrid
raw_findings.trigger: A booking is cancelled/rescheduled shortly (under the ~15-minute CRON interval) before a scheduled reminder's `scheduledDate`, e.g. an attendee cancels 10 minutes before a "1 hour before event" reminder fires; the next CRON run occurs after the send time.

raw_findings.body: Previously the reminder deletions were PrismaPromises collected into `remindersToDelete` and awaited via Promise.all before responding. Now the async delete/update calls are invoked inside forEach without awaiting and are not included in the awaited `prismaPromises`, so the `cancelled: true` update (or row delete) may never commit after the response is sent — the reminder then remains active and the email/SMS is still sent. The same un-awaited pattern was introduced in bookings.tsx requestReschedule and workflows.tsx (where `await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)` was removed).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reminder cancellation state can silently fail to persist, so reminders for cancelled/rescheduled bookings are still delivered.

The same un-awaited pattern was introduced in bookings.tsx requestReschedule and workflows.tsx (where `await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)` was removed).
raw_findings.root_cause: Refactor replaced awaited PrismaPromise batches with un-awaited async function calls inside synchronous forEach loops.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Collect the promises returned by deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder and await them (e.g., Promise.all) before the handler returns, in all touched call sites.
raw_findings.title: Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget; awaited DB cleanup was removed, risking dropped updates in serverless runtime
raw_findings.trigger: Booking cancellation running on a serverless platform (cal.com deploys on Vercel): the handler returns its response while the un-awaited prisma update/delete promises inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are still pending, and the function is frozen.

raw_findings.body: The `log.error` branch can never execute; failures during reminder cancellation are silently swallowed by inner console.log catches, giving reviewers/operators a false impression that this path is monitored.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Misleading, unreachable error-handling code degrades observability and maintainability of the reschedule path.
raw_findings.impact: The `log.error` branch can never execute; failures during reminder cancellation are silently swallowed by inner console.log catches, giving reviewers/operators a false impression that this path is monitored.
raw_findings.root_cause: Error handling was added around fire-and-forget calls whose promises are ignored and whose implementations already swallow all errors.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the dead try/catch, or make the delete functions rethrow/return errors and await them (e.g., `await Promise.all(...)`) so the catch can actually observe failures.
raw_findings.title: try/catch around un-awaited reminder cancellation calls is unreachable dead code
raw_findings.trigger: Any failure inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder during a reschedule: both functions catch all errors internally, and the calls inside forEach are not awaited, so no rejection can propagate to this try block.

raw_findings.title: No tests for the new cancelled-flag branching in deleteScheduledEmailReminder and the CRON cancellation pass
raw_findings.trigger: Any future change to the three branches (null referenceId → row delete, immediateDelete → SendGrid cancel only, default → set cancelled flag) or to the CRON's cancel-then-delete pass in scheduleEmailReminders.ts.

validated_findings.body: This path performs the immediate SendGrid `status: "cancel"` POST that this PR identifies as the root cause of the original bug (pending cancellations accumulate until the scheduled date, capping at 100, after which cancellations fail). When the call fails, nothing marks the row `cancelled` or deletes it, so the CRON never picks it up and the old booking's reminder email is still sent. Even on success, the workflowReminder row is left with `scheduled: true` and no `cancelled` flag until the top-of-CRON deleteMany prunes it.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Rescheduled bookings can still receive stale workflow reminder emails once SendGrid's pending-cancellation limit is hit, silently defeating the fix for this code path.

Per emailReminderManager.ts:213-222, this issues immediate SendGrid cancel without setting cancelled flag or deleting row. If SendGrid fails, row remains with scheduled=true, CRON won't pick it up (no cancelled=true), and email sends. This bypasses the deferred mechanism the PR introduces elsewhere.

validated_findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder only sets `cancelled: true` and relies entirely on the CRON; if the reminder's send time falls before the next CRON execution, the top-of-handler deleteMany (scheduledDate <= now) removes the row without ever issuing the SendGrid cancel, and the reminder email is delivered for a cancelled booking — the exact symptom this PR fixes, now for last-minute cancellations. The previous code cancelled immediately and did not have this window.

validated_findings.root_cause: The new deferred-cancellation design assumes the CRON will always run between the cancellation event and the reminder's send time, which is false for cancellations occurring within one CRON period of the send time.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: In deleteScheduledEmailReminder, additionally issue an immediate SendGrid cancel when scheduledDate is within the CRON interval (or process cancelled reminders before the deleteMany and widen/reorder logic so imminent sends are cancelled synchronously).
validated_findings.title: Reminders cancelled less than one CRON interval before their send time are never cancelled at SendGrid
validated_findings.trigger: A booking is cancelled/rescheduled shortly (under the ~15-minute CRON interval) before a scheduled reminder's `scheduledDate`, e.g. an attendee cancels 10 minutes before a "1 hour before event" reminder fires; the next CRON run occurs after the send time.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 34-41 show deleteMany for scheduledDate <= now runs before the cancellation pass (lines 43-77) which only processes cancelled=true with scheduledDate <= now+1hour. If a booking is cancelled shortly before send time and CRON runs after scheduledDate, the row is deleted by deleteMany before cancellation logic runs, so SendGrid cancel never issued. Edge case but realistic for last-minute cancellations.

validated_findings.body: Previously the reminder deletions were PrismaPromises collected into `remindersToDelete` and awaited via Promise.all before responding. Now the async delete/update calls are invoked inside forEach without awaiting and are not included in the awaited `prismaPromises`, so the `cancelled: true` update (or row delete) may never commit after the response is sent — the reminder then remains active and the email/SMS is still sent. The same un-awaited pattern was introduced in bookings.tsx requestReschedule and workflows.tsx (where `await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)` was removed).
